**Analysis:**

**Test image observations:**
- Green mango leaf on white background
- Small round raised structures (galls) visible along the leaf margins and scattered on the surface
- Some small holes/exit holes visible in the leaf tissue
- Leaf is otherwise intact and not deformed significantly

**Key comparison:**
- **Gall Midge** reference: shows exactly the same pattern — small dark brown/black round galls clustered along leaf margins and scattered on the surface, with shot holes left when galls fall out. The match is very strong.
- **Powdery Mildew**: shows white powdery patches — not present in test image
- **Sooty Mould**: shows dark black encrustation across leaf surface — not present
- **Anthracnose**: shows brown/yellow discoloration and tip damage — not present
- **Cutting_Weevil**: shows stripped shoots with minimal leaf tissue — not matching

The small round raised bumps along the leaf margin and surface in the test image are characteristic galls from Gall Midge, matching the reference images very closely.
